title: Scale Economies
coreMove: Test whether growth bends the unit-cost curve and leaves followers structurally disadvantaged.
sourcePressure: Scale economies are declining unit costs as business size increases. The pressure is benefit plus barrier: volume must lower unit economics and make smaller rivals chase from a worse cost position, not merely make the company larger.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Scale economies mean being big, growing fast, or celebrating market share without proving lower unit cost and a barrier.

sourceAnchors.name: Netflix
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen notes say original content shifted a major expense toward fixed cost, so subscriber scale lowered the per-user burden and made matching harder for smaller streamers
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Netflix matters here because the same show becomes cheaper per subscriber only after the audience is large enough to spread the fixed cost.

sourceAnchors.name: Intel
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar ties Intel to takeoff-stage timing where scale and switching costs can widen advantage in a significant market
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Intel belongs as a timing signal, not a full case history: scale power only helps when the market window is large enough to matter.
